P0800.d: P0800 works like P0700 for the transmission: the transfer case control module has detected a fault of its own that it rates as emissions-relevant and asks the engine control module to turn on the MIL. The engine module only stores P0800; the actual fault – often C, U or manufacturer codes – sits in the transfer case module and needs a scan tool that addresses it.
s: Check engine lamp on
'Service 4WD' or similar warning
All-wheel drive or low range cannot be selected
c: Fault in the transfer case system stored in its module (shift motor, sensor, clutch)
Wiring or connector at the transfer case (terminal tension, corrosion)

P0801.d: On GM manual gearboxes (Tremec T56/TR6060 in Corvette, Camaro, CTS-V and ATS-V) the engine module drives a solenoid that blocks reverse while the car moves forward. P0801 means its control circuit is open.
s: Reverse hard or impossible to engage
Reverse no longer blocked
Service note in the driver display, usually no MIL
c: Connector at the reverse inhibit solenoid loose or corroded
Harness between engine module and gearbox damaged

P0802.d: On older vehicles with a separate transmission module and no MIL message on the CAN bus, the transmission module signals 'MIL on' over its own wire to the engine module. P0802 checks this wire for an open circuit.
s: Check engine lamp on
Transmission faults no longer light the MIL
Usually no change in driving
c: MIL request wire or connector between the modules open or corroded
Transmission module without power or ground (fuse, relay)
Wrong or retrofitted transmission module without this line

P0803.d: GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes such as the T56 and TR6060 uses an engine-module solenoid in the shifter housing that, at light load and low speed blocks the way from 1st into 2nd and 3rd so the driver shifts 1 to 4 – a measure for fuel economy ratings; the 1-4 lamp (P0804) shows it. P0803 means the solenoid control circuit is open.
s: Check engine lamp after two trips
1-4 lockout no longer works (1-2 always possible)
Otherwise no change in driving
c: Solenoid unplugged or replaced by a skip-shift eliminator with the wrong resistance
Connector at the gearbox loose or corroded

P0804.d: With GM's skip-shift (CAGS) on manual gearboxes, a '1-4' lamp in the cluster tells the driver that the lockout is active and to shift from 1st directly into 4th. P0804 means the control circuit of this lamp is faulty – open, shorted, or the lamp does not follow its command.
s: 1-4 lamp never lights or stays on
Possibly check engine lamp
Lockout works without the hint
c: Bulb or LED in the cluster faulty
Wire or connector between engine module and cluster open or shorted

P0805.d: The J2012 family 'Clutch Position Sensor A' (P0805 circuit, P0806 range/performance, P0807 low, P0808 high, P0809 intermittent, P080A not learned) covers the position of a clutch – the pedal of a manual gearbox, the clutch actuator of an automated or dual-clutch gearbox, or a clutch inside an automatic. P0805 is the general circuit fault.
s: Check engine lamp on
Idle stop disabled ('Idle Stop System Fault')
Jerky driving or harsh clutch engagement (dual clutch)
c: Clutch position sensor faulty (pedal or actuator)
Connector or harness open, corroded or shorted
Control unit internal fault (Ford DPS6: clutch motor driver)

P0806.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. GM used P0806–P080A until model year 2018 for the analog clutch pedal sensor of its manual cars, then the newer pedal sensor codes P08A8 ff; Saab's 2012 9-3 does the same.
s: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control and start-stop not working
Engine starts only with the pedal fully pressed, or not at all
Dual clutch: jerky take-off, limp mode
c: Pedal sensor or Hall sensors of the clutch motor faulty
Pedal sensor misadjusted or not relearned after clutch work
Harness or connector with contact resistance
Master cylinder leaking, pedal does not fully return

P0807.d: The 'Clutch Position Sensor A' family (P0805 circuit to P0809, P080A not learned) means different parts by vehicle generation. s: Check engine lamp on
Cruise control not working
Start-stop disabled, possibly no engine start

5 V reference of the sensor missing

The engine module drives the solenoid with a low-side driver; P0803 is the open circuit.

1-4 lockout works not at all or only sometimes
Otherwise no change in driving

Retrofitted skip-shift eliminator with the wrong value
Corroded connector at the gearbox (contact resistance)

P0810.d: P0810 reports a control error of an electronically or hydraulically operated clutch: commanded and actual position differ too much or for too long. It is documented on Stellantis plug-in hybrids – Jeep Wrangler 4xe and Grand Cherokee 4xe with the 8P75PH transmission – where it concerns the K0 disconnect clutch between engine and electric motor.
s: Check engine lamp on
Transmission warning message
Loss of drive until the next key cycle
c: Control unit software with too tight parameters
Clutch actuator or hydraulics (pressure, valve) faulty
Wrong or aged fluid, worn clutch

P0811.d: P0811 means clutch A slips too much while it should be closed – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 1 with the odd gears. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch; thresholds are not published.
s: Transmission warning, limp mode
Engine flares, poor acceleration
Judder on take-off
Burning smell
c: Transmission module calculating wrong slip (speed capture)
Clutch pressure or actuator too low

P0812.d: P0812 concerns the input 'reverse engaged' at the engine or transmission module – the reverse or back-up lamp switch on a manual gearbox, or the R contact of a selector. Modules check it for open or stuck states and against a second source such as a gear position sensor or the direction from speed sensors.
s: Back-up lamps never or always on
Reversing camera or parking aid does not switch on
Usually no check engine lamp
c: Reverse or back-up lamp switch faulty or misadjusted
Connector loose or wire broken (e.g. after clutch work)
Gear position sensor reporting the wrong position

P0813.d: P0813 concerns a signal 'reverse active' that a module puts out – usually the transmission module, on manual cars the engine or body module – for example to the back-up lamp relay, the reversing camera or the body module. Like other driver outputs it is checked by comparing commanded and actual state, which reveals an open circuit or a short.
s: Back-up lamps not working
Reversing camera or parking beeper does not activate
Stored code without driving effects
c: Wire from module to relay or body module open or shorted
Back-up lamp relay or connected load faulty

s: Range display on the selector flickers or stays dark
Check engine lamp (Jeep)
Lever can leave P during cranking, engine stalls (Jeep)
c: Connector or wire to the selector display or cluster
Display LED or selector module faulty
Range sensor or transmission module delivering an invalid range

P0815.d: Tap-up and tap-down switches let the driver choose gears on an automatic (selector gate, buttons or paddles). GM, Ford and Saab all treat a shift request that appears where it is impossible – in park or neutral, at Ford also reverse – or that stays on implausibly long as a stuck switch.

Transmission stays in the normal automatic mode
No check engine lamp
c: Tap switch or paddle sticking or faulty
Selector assembly (Hall sensor, resistor network) faulty

P0817.d: The starter disable line carries the signal 'park or neutral – start allowed' from the transmission module, or its built-in range switch, to the body or engine module, which only then releases the starter. On Saab's 2010 9-5 automatic the line is open in a drive range (0 V at the body module) and closed in P or N (12 V).

Start possible in only one of the two ranges
No check engine lamp
c: Starter disable wire to the body module open or shorted
Connector corroded or pins pushed back
Transmission module with built-in range switch faulty

s: All-wheel drive or neutral cannot be selected
'Service 4WD' or similar warning

P0819.d: P0819 is the plausibility check between the tap-up and tap-down switches and the range sensor: a shift request may only appear in the manual gate or in drive. If a tap switch reports in P, R or N, or taps arrive without the manual gate being detected, the correlation is broken.

Range display partly wrong
No check engine lamp
c: Range sensor or selector sensor misadjusted or faulty

P081D.d: P081D concerns the input 'neutral' – the N contact of the selector or range switch, on manual cars a neutral switch or sensor for start-stop. Neutral serves for starter release, idle control without load, start-stop release and enabling other diagnostics.

Start-stop not working
Range display does not show N

P081E.d: P081E is the counterpart to P0811 for clutch B – on a dual-clutch gearbox clutch 2 with the even gears and reverse, which Audi calls 'clutch 2'. The module compares engine speed with the input shaft speed of the closed clutch and flags slip above its limit.

P081F.d: The brake transmission shift interlock (BTSI) is a solenoid or actuator that locks the selector in park until the brake pedal is pressed, as US rule FMVSS 114 requires. 'Signal correlation' is the plausibility check between the interlock command or feedback and its input signals – brake switch and selector position: for example the lock released without a brake signal, or still active although the brake is pressed.
s: Selector cannot be moved out of P
Selector moves out of P without the brake
Warning about brake or range
c: Brake lamp switch misadjusted or faulty
Interlock solenoid or locking mechanism sticking
Wire or connector to the selector
Selector module, control unit or software

Missing supply or ground for sensor B
Faulty sensor B input in the engine control module

P08B5.d: P08B5 covers a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal lies within its electrical limits but is implausible on its own, for example stuck at one value while the pedal moves or not matching the driving state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop or cruise control unavailable
c: Sensor B drifting or worn so its value no longer follows pedal travel
Sensor loose or misaligned on the pedal bracket
Corrosion adding resistance in the sensor B circuit

P08B6.d: P08B6 means the signal of the second clutch pedal sensor has dropped below its valid range. Ford lists it in the 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary under dual PWM clutch sensors, together with P08A9/P08AA for sensor A, P08B7 for sensor B high and P08B9 for the A/B comparison; monitoring runs continuously and needs less than one second to flag a fault.
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
P08B9 correlation code may set alongside
c: Sensor B signal wire shorted to ground
Lost supply voltage to sensor B (open wire, connector off)
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B

P08B7.d: P08B7 is set when the second clutch pedal sensor reports a value above its valid range. Ford uses it on vehicles with two PWM clutch pedal sensors, as listed in its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary next to P08B6 (sensor B low), P08A9/P08AA (sensor A) and P08B9 (A/B correlation); the check is continuous and decides within one second.
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Sensor B reading pinned at maximum in scan tool data
c: Open signal or ground wire of sensor B, leaving the input at its pull-up level
Sensor B signal shorted to a voltage source
Failed clutch pedal position sensor B

P08B8.d: P08B8 is intended for a second clutch pedal sensor whose signal drops out briefly or jumps without staying out of range. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Start-stop dropping out intermittently
Warning lamp that comes and goes
c: Loose or worn terminals in the sensor B connector
Wire fatiguing where the harness flexes with pedal movement

P08B9.d: P08B9 is stored when two independent measurements of the clutch pedal disagree. Ford uses it in two ways per its 2020–23 gasoline OBD summary: with dual PWM sensors it compares sensor A with sensor B and decides within a second; with a single analog sensor plus two clutch switches it covers an in-range rationality fault or any switch-related mismatch, the switch part being judged over about 40 clutch cycles at differ
s: Warning lamp on
Start-stop disabled
Cruise control unavailable
c: One of the two sensors drifting or worn so the channels no longer agree
Sticking or misadjusted clutch switch on systems with one sensor plus switches
Corroded connector or wiring adding resistance to one channel
Sensor assembly or pedal stop misaligned after repairs

P08BA.d: Base code for the twelfth pressure control solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve carries the letter L is up to the manufacturer. Toyota is the one documented user: bulletin T-SB-0094-24 for the 2024 Tacoma and Tacoma Hybrid lists it as P08BA71, actuator stuck, next to the stuck faults of solenoids A, C, D, G and H and a torque converter clutch stuck off.
s: Check engine light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear
c: Solenoid or its control valve sticking inside the valve body
Internal transmission fault from production, debris spreading through the hydraulics
Connector or harness fault at the solenoid

P08BB.d: Set when pressure control solenoid L is commanded but the pressure or shift element it serves does not respond, i.e. the valve acts as if it were stuck in its off state.
s: Check engine light on
Missing, slipping or delayed shifts
Possible substitute gear operation
c: Valve spool held closed by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Leaking seal or circuit downstream of the valve

P08BC.d: Set when pressure control solenoid L keeps applying pressure although the control module has commanded it off, so the element it feeds stays loaded. No manufacturer publishes this code.
s: Check engine light on
Harsh engagement or binding during shifts
Transmission locked in a fallback gear
c: Valve spool held open by debris
Worn bore in the valve body letting pressure through
Output stage or wiring keeping the solenoid energised

P08BD.d: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid L that the module does not break down further into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly; Toyota, the one known user of letter L, has only published the stuck fault P08BA71.
s: Check engine light on
Restricted gears or fallback gear
c: Corroded connector or damaged internal harness
Faulty output stage in the transmission control module

P08BE.d: Reports a fault of pressure control solenoid L that comes and goes, typically a circuit that drops out briefly or a valve response that is only occasionally implausible. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and in earlier packages the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids also proved unused.
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or flaring shift
c: Loose or spread terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector
Debris making the valve hang only now and then

P08BF.d: Points to an open control circuit of pressure control solenoid L: the module sees no load where the coil should be. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only known user of letter L, has published just P08BA71.
s: Check engine light on
Transmission in fallback gear
c: Broken wire in the internal or external harness

P08C0.d: Set when the control circuit of pressure control solenoid L is electrically intact but its behaviour is implausible, for example the current through the coil does not match the commanded value. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the only documented user of letter L, publishes only P08BA71.
s: Check engine light on
Uneven shift quality
c: High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module

P08C1.d: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too low, usually a short to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71.
s: Check engine light on
Transmission in fallback gear
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil
Fluid or moisture in the connector

P08C2.d: Reports a control circuit voltage of pressure control solenoid L that is too high, typically a short to battery voltage or to a neighbouring output. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; Toyota, the one documented user of letter L, has published only P08BA71.
s: Check engine light on
Transmission in fallback gear
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short between adjacent solenoid wires in the internal harness
Defective output stage in the transmission control module

P08C3.d: Base code for the thirteenth pressure control solenoid; the letter is assigned by the manufacturer. GM uses letter M in the Tremec eight-speed dual clutch of the Corvette (RPO M1L/M1M): its 2023–2025 TCM tables name the part synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft, while valves 2 to 5 report under P27B9 onwards.
s: Check engine light on
Rough or missing shifts in odd gears
Possible fallback mode
c: Valve sticking from debris in the valve body
Fault in the solenoid wiring or connector

P08C4.d: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft, is hydraulically stuck off. The test runs inside a synchronizer recovery or integrity routine, started after a shift-related fault or when the stored gear does not match the sensed gears at start-up: the shift rods are moved slightly, and if a rod travels 100 µm or less where the valve should
s: Check engine light on
Odd gears not engaged or engaged late
Noise from the transmission area
c: Valve stuck closed by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Low system pressure or fluid level

P08C5.d: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch when synchronizer actuation valve 1, serving the odd-gear shaft, keeps pressure on although it is commanded off. The check runs whenever the selector pilot valve changes position: a valve stuck on keeps pushing a shift rod, so after the switch the pressure is routed elsewhere.
s: Check engine light on
Clunks or unwanted gear engagement on the odd shaft
Noise from the transmission area
c: Valve held open by debris in the control valve body
Debris from a dislodged snap ring in the direct clutch assembly (bulletin 23-NA-197)
Worn valve bore in the control valve body

P08C6.d: Collective code for an electrical fault of pressure control solenoid M without a finer split into open, low or high. No manufacturer documents it publicly.
s: Check engine light on
Restricted shifting or fallback mode
c: Faulty driver stage in the transmission control module

P08C7.d: Reports an on-and-off fault of pressure control solenoid M, such as brief circuit dropouts or occasional implausible responses. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM, which uses letter M for synchronizer actuation valve 1 of the Corvette dual clutch, lists no intermittent code for it, and earlier packages found the intermittent codes of the other pressure control solenoids unused as well.
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Sporadic rough shifts
c: Loose terminal at the solenoid or transmission connector

P08C8.d: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for an open circuit at synchronizer actuation valve 1, the valve for the odd-gear shaft. The open-load test runs with the low-side driver switched off: an intact coil pulls the sense pin to battery voltage, so if the driver chip can hold it between about 1.7 and 3 V (each ±0.5 V) with a very small current, the circuit is considered open.
s: Check engine light on immediately
Fallback mode with restricted gears
c: Connector at the control valve body loose or corroded
Broken wire in the internal harness

P08C9.d: Meant for a control circuit of pressure control solenoid M that is not open or shorted but behaves implausibly, for instance a coil current that does not follow the command. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine light on
Uneven shift quality
c: High contact resistance at connector pins
Unstable supply voltage to the transmission module

P08CA.d: GM sets this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for a short to ground in the circuit of synchronizer actuation valve 1, which serves the odd-gear shaft. The test runs while the low-side driver is switched on: the sense pin should then sit at a defined level, and if the driver chip reports it below about 1.7 V (±0.5 V), a ground short is assumed.
s: Check engine light on immediately
Fallback mode with restricted gears
c: Control wire chafed through to ground
Shorted turns in the solenoid coil

P08CB.d: GM uses this code on the Corvette's Tremec dual clutch for synchronizer actuation valve 1 (odd-gear shaft) in two situations. First, a short to battery voltage: with the low-side driver on, a sense voltage above 0.7, 0.9 or 1.1 V (±0.1 V), depending on supply voltage, counts as a shorted load, confirmed after 150 ms.
s: Check engine light on immediately
Fallback mode with restricted gears
Code may appear right after starting
c: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Short to an adjacent solenoid wire in the internal harness
Defective driver stage in the transmission control module

P08CC.d: Base code for the tenth on/off shift solenoid of an automatic transmission; which valve gets the letter J is decided by the manufacturer. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear
c: Shift solenoid J faulty (coil or valve)
Contaminated or degraded transmission fluid restricting the valve
Connector or harness fault between TCM and solenoid

P08CD.d: Set when shift solenoid J is switched on but the gear or clutch it controls does not respond, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare or slipping during or after a shift
A gear is missing or skipped
Transmission may hold a substitute gear
c: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the off position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak supply pressure to the valve
Worn clutch pack or leaking seal in the circuit served by the valve
Solenoid coil too weak to move the valve

P08CE.d: Set when shift solenoid J is switched off but its clutch or shift valve stays applied, so the valve behaves as if stuck in its on position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement, possible binding feel
Transmission goes into limp mode
c: Solenoid or its shift valve held in the applied position by debris or varnish
Contaminated transmission fluid after internal wear
Control circuit shorted so the solenoid stays energised
TCM output driver does not switch off

P08CF.d: General electrical fault of shift solenoid J, used when a manufacturer does not split the circuit fault into open, low, high or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or missing shifts
Transmission may lock into a limp-home gear
c: Solenoid coil open or shorted internally
Damaged harness, corroded or loose connector at the transmission
Fault in the internal transmission harness or solenoid body

P08D0.d: Reserved for a shift solenoid J fault that comes and goes instead of being present continuously, typically brief circuit dropouts or erratic valve response. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the intermittent codes of the earlier shift solenoids, such as P0754 for solenoid A, are not used in the GM and Ford sources checked either; those makers report dropouts through their open, short or functional cod
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or delayed shifts
Sporadic limp mode that clears after restart
c: Loose or corroded connector losing contact under vibration or heat
Chafed harness with intermittent short or break
Valve sticking now and then due to contaminated fluid
Solenoid coil failing only when hot

P08D1.d: Set when the control circuit of shift solenoid J is electrically intact but its measured values, usually solenoid current or driver feedback, lie outside the expected window for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or irregular shifts
Possible limp mode
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
High resistance at connector pins or internal harness
Unstable supply voltage to the TCM or solenoid feed
Faulty current sensing in the TCM output stage

P08D2.d: Set when the TCM sees too little voltage on the control line of shift solenoid J, typically because the line or the coil is shorted to ground. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; J would be a tenth on/off valve, which none of the known transmission sources assigns.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission holds a substitute gear
Harsh or missing shifts
c: Control wire chafed through and shorted to ground
Damaged internal transmission harness or lead frame
Faulty output stage in the TCM

P08D3.d: Logged when the control line of shift solenoid J reads higher than the commanded state allows, pointing to a short to battery voltage or, on some designs, an open coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement
Possible limp mode
c: Control wire shorted to a voltage-carrying conductor
Open solenoid coil (on systems that report opens as high)
Moisture in the transmission connector bridging pins

P08D4.d: Dedicated code for an open control circuit of shift solenoid J: the TCM drives the valve but no current flows through wire, connector or coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
One gear missing or transmission stuck in one gear
Harsh shifts
c: Broken control wire or loose terminal
Transmission connector not fully seated after service

P08D5.d: Base code for shift solenoid K, the eleventh on/off shift valve in SAE's lettering. Which valve carries the letter is up to the manufacturer, and none documents K publicly: Ford's gasoline OBD summary lists shift solenoids only up to SS E, Hyundai's bulletin 21-AT-016HG for the Genesis 8-speed ends at shift control solenoid F, and GM's 2016 to 2025 tables contain no code of the K group.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, delayed or missing shifts
Transmission may hold a substitute gear
c: Shift solenoid K faulty (coil or valve)
Harness or connector fault between TCM and solenoid

P08D6.d: Indicates that shift solenoid K was commanded on but the gear or clutch behind it never engaged, as if the valve stayed in its off position. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare or slipping during shifts
A gear is skipped or missing
c: Valve or shift spool held in rest position by debris or varnish
Low fluid level or weak line pressure
Leaking seal or worn clutch pack in the circuit fed by the valve

P08D7.d: Stored when shift solenoid K is switched off but the circuit it feeds stays pressurised, so a clutch remains applied. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear when pulling away
Binding or harsh engagement
Limp mode
c: Valve or shift spool jammed in applied position
Metal debris in the fluid after internal wear
TCM output or shorted wire keeps the solenoid energised

P08D8.d: Collective electrical fault for shift solenoid K, used by makers that do not split circuit faults into low, high, open or range codes. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or missing shifts
Transmission may lock into a limp-home gear

P08D9.d: Meant for a shift solenoid K fault that appears and vanishes, such as a connector losing contact over bumps or a coil dropping out when hot. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and none of the sources checked even uses the intermittent code of solenoid A, P0754; GM and Ford catch brief interruptions with their open, short and functional codes instead.
s: Warning light that comes and goes
Occasional harsh or late shift
Sporadic limp mode that clears after restart
c: Loose or fretted terminal in the transmission connector
Chafed wire that touches only under vibration
Solenoid coil dropping out at high fluid temperature

P08DA.d: Points to a control circuit of shift solenoid K that is neither open nor shorted, yet whose measured values, usually coil current, do not fit the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the analogue for solenoid A, P0972, is not used in the GM or Ford sources either.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Delayed or soft shifts
Possible limp mode
c: Solenoid coil resistance out of specification
Corroded or loose pins adding resistance
TCM output stage no longer delivers correct current

P08DB.d: The TCM's output stage reports a voltage on the shift solenoid K control circuit below what the commanded state requires, the classic sign of a control wire rubbing through to ground or a coil with an internal short. No manufacturer documents this K code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission stays in a limp-home gear
Reduced acceleration due to missing gears
c: Control wire rubbed through to ground

P08DC.d: The monitored control line of shift solenoid K sits closer to supply voltage than it should, for instance because it touches a powered wire or, depending on the driver design, because the coil is open. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear or harsh engagement
Possible limp mode
c: Control wire touching a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high
TCM low-side driver no longer pulls the line down

P08DD.d: Signals that the control circuit of shift solenoid K is open, so commanding the valve produces no current: a broken wire, a pushed-out terminal, a burnt coil or a failed internal transmission harness. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Some gears no longer available
Limp mode with fixed gear

P08DE.d: Base code for shift solenoid L, which in SAE's lettering would be the twelfth on/off shift valve of an automatic transmission. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh or erratic shifting
Possible substitute gear
c: Wiring or connector fault on the solenoid circuit
Debris in the valve body affecting the valve

P08DF.d: Functional fault of shift solenoid L: the TCM switches the valve on, but speed sensor data show that the intended clutch did not take up, so the valve acts as if stuck off. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Engine flare between gears
Gear missing or skipped
c: Low line pressure or low fluid level
Leak in the clutch circuit fed by the valve

P08E0.d: Functional fault of shift solenoid L in the opposite direction: although switched off, the valve keeps its circuit applied, leaving engaged a clutch that should be released. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Drivetrain binding or harsh shifts
Limp mode
c: Shift spool seized in applied position
Contaminated fluid after clutch or bearing wear
TCM output stage does not switch off

P08E1.d: General electrical malfunction of shift solenoid L, intended for transmissions whose TCM does not distinguish or separately report low, high and open circuit faults. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh shifts or fixed gear
Reduced driving performance
c: Harness or connector damage on the solenoid circuit

P08E2.d: Reserved for an unstable fault of shift solenoid L that is detected, disappears and may return, typically from a loose terminal, a chafed wire that only touches under vibration or a heat-sensitive coil. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Intermittent warning light
Occasional harsh shift
Limp mode that disappears after restart
c: Loose terminal or poor pin tension in the connector
Insulation chafed at a bracket or edge
Coil that fails intermittently when hot

P08E3.d: Plausibility fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L: the circuit is not open or shorted, but voltage or current during actuation is implausible for the commanded state. No manufacturer documents this code publicly, and the matching code for solenoid A, P0972, is likewise absent from the GM and Ford documents checked.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Soft or delayed shifts
Possible limp mode
c: TCM output stage losing drive strength

P08E4.d: Low-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L. Usually it means a short to ground on the control wire, less often a coil with shorted windings that pulls the voltage down.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Transmission locked in a substitute gear
Weak acceleration
c: Fluid or moisture in the connector creating a path to ground

P08E5.d: High-voltage fault in the control circuit of shift solenoid L, set when the line shows battery voltage or a floating high level while the TCM expects otherwise. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Wrong gear selected
Harsh engagement or limp mode
c: Control wire chafed against a powered conductor
Open coil on systems that read opens as high

P08E6.d: Open circuit in the control path of shift solenoid L: harness, connector, internal transmission wiring or the coil itself no longer carry current, so the valve cannot be energised. No manufacturer documents this code publicly.
s: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Gear range missing or fixed gear
Harsh shifts
c: Break in the harness or internal transmission wiring
Connector unlatched or terminal backed out

P08E7.d: Covers the enable line with which a drive motor control module activates the actuator of a clutch that couples or uncouples electric drive motor A from the wheels. The code sets when the module sees an electrical fault on that line, typically an open circuit or an implausible state.
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
No electric drive or assist from the affected axle
All-wheel-drive or electric-only modes unavailable
c: Enable wire open or connector at the clutch actuator not seated
Internal electronics fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Corroded or water-damaged connector near the drive unit
Faulty enable driver in the drive motor control module

P08E8.d: Set when the voltage on the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator stays below the expected range, usually because the wire or the actuator input is shorted to ground. The control module can then no longer switch the actuator on, so the clutch cannot be engaged or released on command.
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive axle stays disconnected
Reduced performance, no electric launch or all-wheel drive
c: Enable wire chafed and shorted to ground
Internal short at the actuator enable input
Water ingress in the actuator connector
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module

P08E9.d: Set when the enable line of the drive motor A disconnect clutch actuator reads higher than it should, for example because it is shorted to a supply voltage or the line floats due to an open ground. The module then cannot reliably switch the actuator off or confirm its state.
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive on the affected axle switched off
Possible clunk when the system tries to couple the motor
c: Enable wire shorted to a supply circuit
Open ground or reference circuit of the actuator
Internal fault in the disconnect clutch actuator
Faulty output stage in the drive motor control module

P08EA.d: Concerns the sensor or switch that reports where the pawl of the drive motor A disconnect clutch sits, i.e. whether the form-locking clutch is engaged or released.
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive or all-wheel drive unavailable
Reduced acceleration in hybrid modes
c: Faulty disconnect clutch position switch or sensor
Open signal or reference wire to the position switch
Corroded or loose connector at the drive unit
Faulty input stage in the drive motor control module

P08EB.d: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays below its valid range, which points to a short to ground in the signal wire, a missing sensor supply or a sensor that has failed low. The module then cannot tell whether the pawl has engaged.
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
Electric drive axle disabled
Hybrid modes with electric assist not selectable
c: Position signal wire shorted to ground
Missing supply voltage to the position switch
Position switch or sensor failed low

P08EC.d: Set when the pawl position signal of the drive motor A disconnect clutch stays above its valid range. Typical reasons are an open signal or ground wire, which lets the input float high, or a short to a supply voltage.
s: Check engine light or hybrid system warning on
No electric drive from the affected axle
All-wheel drive or electric launch missing
c: Open signal or ground wire of the position switch
Signal wire shorted to a supply circuit
Position switch or sensor failed high

P08ED.d: A plausibility fault: the pawl position reported for the drive motor A disconnect clutch does not match what the control module commanded, or the clutch did not reach the expected position, even though the circuit itself is electrically intact. GM documents the code for the 2024 Corvette E-Ray, whose front electric drive unit uses a clutch pawl and a disconnect clutch actuator; bulletin 24-NA-165 says it is stored in
s: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Electric front-axle drive unavailable or intermittent
Hybrid modes restricted
c: Faulty drive motor disconnect clutch switch (GM E-Ray bulletin)
Disconnect clutch actuator not moving the pawl fully
Worn or binding pawl or clutch teeth inside the drive unit
